headline: The US military secretly made it rain on purpose during the Vietnam War.
slides: Operation Popeye began: planes seeded clouds over the Ho Chi Minh Trail with silver and lead iodide.
Stretch the monsoon season, turn supply roads to mud and wash out river crossings.
The squadron's motto was 'make mud, not war.'
Missions flew every rainy season for five years, from bases in Thailand.
Officials told Congress no weather-war program existed.
A New York Times report exposed it, and it was shut down. In 1977 a UN treaty banned weather as a weapon.
sources: Sources: US Senate hearings on weather modification (1974), NYT (July 3 1972), ENMOD Convention (1977)
